title: The ramification least-common-multiple conjecture for surface algebras
statement:
Let $R$ be a coefficient ring or field of positive characteristic, let $G$ be a finite group obtained from the pullback of the two local Galois-theoretic constructions, and let $\sigma_r$ and $\sigma_s$ be automorphisms mapped to primitive $r^{\text{th}}$ and $s^{\text{th}}$ roots of unity, respectively. Let the ramification degrees over $x_r$ and $x_s$ be the corresponding degrees associated with these automorphisms. The group ring $RG$ decomposes into blocks

$$
RG=B_1\oplus\cdots\oplus B_l.
$$

**Ramification least-common-multiple conjecture.** The least common multiple of the orders of $\sigma_r$ and $\sigma_s$ should have significant meaning in modular representation theory; more specifically, the least common multiple of the ramification degrees over $x_r$ and $x_s$ should yield a relation in the surface algebra of the same type as a relation in the definition of a Brauer graph algebra. Appropriate quotients of surface algebras should thereby yield Brauer graph algebras.

This proposes a connection between pullback constructions, modular representation theory, surface algebras, and Brauer graph algebras. The source gives no evidence that the proposed relation or the resulting quotient construction has been proved, so its resolution remains unclear.
source_name: Amelie Schreiber, “Surface Algebras and Surface Orders II: Affine Bundles on Curves”, arXiv:1812.00621 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.00621

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2018).
